question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Particle and the Origin
question.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(2i-4j)\,\text{m},$ with an acceleration of $(-i+j)\,{\text{m/min}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(3i-j)\,\text{m/min}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $6$ minutes.
question.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=2i-4j,\,u=3i-j,\,a=-i+j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=6\,\text{min}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(2i-4j)+(3i-j)(6)+\frac{1}{2}(-i+j)(6)^{2} \\  & =(2i-4j)+(18i-6j)+18(-i+j) \\  & =(20i-10j)+(-18i+18j) \\  & =(2i+8j)\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the particle to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|2i+8j| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64} \\  & =\sqrt{68} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$
